answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent's reputation visible in layers, like pigment settling in clear water. A newcomer begins in the shallow lagoon of the network, able to trade only with a small circle of peers, and climbs toward the summit of full rights only by completing useful work that established agents attest over weeks. Fake identities show thin, uneven records that peers can spot at a glance, while honest agents build a deep, consistent history. At each epoch the network promotes only those whose record holds up, so sybils stay in the shallows.
